observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a sewing machine's needle and presser-foot area. A green-and-white striped fabric lies under the lowered presser foot. A person's right hand rests flat on the fabric to the right of the foot, fingers spread, holding it steady. A warm light pool falls across the fabric. The machine head is visible at the top edge; the background (machine body and operator's dark clothing) stays roughly fixed.
visible_changes: The striped fabric advances continuously under the stationary presser foot; its stripe pattern shifts position relative to the foot from the first to the last frame, indicating active feeding/stitching.
The right hand stays in essentially the same place throughout, guiding from the right side.

At the start the left side of the frame shows only a forearm/wrist not touching the fabric; around t=0.8s the left hand enters from the left and its thumb presses down on the fabric just left of the foot.

The left hand repeatedly adjusts: it briefly lifts and repositions (motion-blurred around t=1.36-1.6s and again from t=2.56s onward), sometimes pulling or smoothing the striped edge, sometimes withdrawing out of view.
Near the end (t=3.0-3.2s) the left hand is raised toward the upper-left and no longer contacts the fabric, while the right hand and the fabric feed continue.
The presser foot remains lowered the whole time; the needle shaft shows slight vertical motion blur in places, consistent with the machine running.
outside_clip_unknowns: When sewing began or will end, and the overall garment/piece being made.
What lies beyond the cropped frame (full machine, pattern being followed).
Whether the left hand's adjustments create intentional gathering or merely guide the fabric.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: the framing is mostly static with possible slight handheld jitter, so the apparent drift of the light patch may be fabric movement rather than camera movement.
Exact phase of the needle (up/down) cannot be reliably read from the stills.
Whether foreground fabric bunching is feed accumulation or active ruching is not fully distinguishable.
